frases: Pick two of three letters: are there six ways, or only [+three]?
It comes down to one question: {show lados}does order matter?
In a {show p}permutation, yes: {show ab}AB and BA are [+different].
In a {show c}combination, no: {swap ab}they are the same.

elementos.text: P(3,2) = 6: AB BA AC CA BC CB

frases: To count permutations: {show fp}n factorial over n minus r, factorial.
With three letters taken two at a time, you get {show ep}[+six].
In the permutations, each pair showed up [-twice].
For combinations, you also {show fc}divide by r factorial.
So each group counts only once: you get {show ec}[+three].
That is the whole difference: {show b}{boom b +0.3}dividing by r factorial.
For the exam, [+remember]: if {show fl1}order matters, permutation; if {show fl2}it does not, combination.
lineas: order does not matter → combination: divide by r!
